title: Incident-bot: phase-based status update prompts + template snippets (with migration + tests)
author: Devon Price
description:
Context: As part of the Status page transparency upgrades project, oncall updates have been inconsistent across incident phases (investigating/identified/monitoring/resolved) and often miss key fields customers ask for (what’s impacted, mitigations/workarounds, and when the next update will be). This PR adds phase-based prompts in incident-bot for status page updates and injects copy-ready template snippets aligned to the agreed comms guidance. It also includes a small config migration (new template bundle + per-phase required fields) and unit tests covering prompt selection, required-field enforcement, and rendering rules.

What’s in this PR (high level): - Adds a phase-aware “Status Update” flow: the bot asks for the incident phase and then guides the user through a structured set of fields (Impact, Affected components, Customer mitigation/workarounds, What we’re doing, Next update time). - Template snippet library keyed by phase (Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved) with customer-safe language + uncertainty phrasing. - Guardrails: prevent publishing an empty/low-information update; requires at least one of {impact, mitigation/workaround, next_update_time} to be present before the bot will produce a draft suitable for posting (posting is still manual in this PR). - Adds “next update time” as a first-class field; supports explicit timestamps and relative suggestions (e.g., “in 30 minutes”), but stores/prints as an ISO timestamp to reduce ambiguity. - Migration: introduces `templates/status_page_updates.v2.yaml` and deprecates the old `templates/status_page_updates.yaml` (still supported with a fallback for 2 releases). - Unit tests for: phase detection/selection, template rendering, required field validation, and migration fallback behavior.

User-visible behavior: - When running `/incident update-status` the bot will now prompt: (1) phase selection, (2) impact summary, (3) components (multi-select), (4) mitigation/workaround (optional), (5) next update time (recommended; required for Sev1+ if provided by incident metadata), then (6) produces a draft status page update text the oncall can copy into the status page UI. - The draft includes a short standardized “Next update by …” line when provided.

Notes / non-goals: - This PR does NOT wire incident state transitions to the status page (draft sync is in PR #317). - This PR does NOT change severity definitions; it consumes existing incident metadata if present. - The text is intentionally conservative: no provider or exploit/vulnerability-like detail, no customer identifiers.

Files / areas changed: - src/commands/update_status.ts: new guided prompt flow and phase selection - src/templates/status_page/v2.ts + templates/status_page_updates.v2.yaml: new template bundle + renderer - src/validation/status_update.ts: required-field checks + next_update_time parsing/normalization - src/config/migrations/2025_06_status_templates_v2.ts: config migration + backwards-compatible fallback - test/update_status.spec.ts, test/templates/status_page_v2.spec.ts, test/migrations/status_templates_v2.spec.ts: coverage for prompts/rendering/migration

Illustrative snippet (rendered draft): Investigating: We’re investigating reports of elevated error rates affecting Streaming responses. Affected components: Streaming (Hosted API), API Gateway (Hosted API). Customer impact: Some requests may disconnect mid-stream or fail with 5xx. What we’re doing: We’re reviewing recent deploys and isolating the failure mode; mitigations are in progress. Customer mitigation/workaround: If possible, retry with exponential backoff; consider temporarily disabling streaming or falling back to non-streaming responses. Next update: by 2025-06-24 17:30 UTC.

Rollout: - Ship behind config: `status_update_templates_version: v2` (default off in this PR; can be enabled per environment). - Fallback path continues to use v1 templates if v2 config is missing.

Testing: - Unit tests added/updated (see list above). - Manual: ran through flows in staging Slack workspace with mock incidents (Sev2 + Sev1) to confirm required fields, timestamp handling, and output formatting.

Docs/ops: - Adds migration notes in `docs/migrations/2025-06-status-templates-v2.md` including how to enable v2 and how to override template strings.

Related: ENG-4824 (guided prompts), ENG-4830 (guardrails), ENG-4831 (investigating copy improvements). Follow-ups in PR #317/#319 for draft-sync and post-incident summary workflow.
commits: feat(update-status): add phase-based guided prompts and field collection
feat(templates): introduce status page update templates v2 + renderer
feat(validation): enforce minimum info + normalize next_update_time to UTC
chore(config): add migration + v1 fallback + docs
test: unit tests for prompt flow, rendering, and migration behavior
review_conversation:
Miles Thornton (review): The flow looks good. Two questions: (1) Can we ensure the bot doesn’t output “Identified” language unless we’re actually confident? (2) For next update time, can we standardize to UTC and make it explicit in the text?

Devon Price (author): (1) Yep — templates are strictly keyed by selected phase, and I tightened the “Identified” snippet to avoid over-claiming. Added a line that we’ll share more details as we confirm scope. (2) Done — all timestamps are normalized to UTC and the rendered string includes “UTC”. Added tests for local inputs.

Rafael Mendes (review): For Sev1+ we need to push on “next update time” even if the oncall doesn’t have a workaround yet. Right now it’s “recommended”; can we make it required when severity >= Sev1 and phase != Resolved?

Devon Price (author): Implemented: if incident metadata includes severity Sev1/Sev0 and phase is Investigating/Identified/Monitoring, the prompt requires a next update time (can be “in 30m” etc). For Sev2+ it remains recommended. Added unit test covering severity gating.

Tomáš Novák (review): Can we avoid internal-ish component names leaking? E.g., ‘scheduler’ isn’t customer-facing. Where does component list come from?

Devon Price (author): Component options are pulled from the status-page component registry config (customer-facing strings only). This PR doesn’t add new components; it only supports multi-select and prints the configured display names.

Kira Thompson (review): Language is generally good. Small tweaks: add explicit “retry with exponential backoff” phrasing and keep mitigation bullets short. Also ensure we never instruct customers to disable security features.

Devon Price (author): Applied copy edits in v2 templates and added a “safe mitigation guidelines” comment in the template doc. No security-disabling guidance is included.

Dr. Aisha Rahman (review): Please confirm we don’t include provider names, exploit details, or customer identifiers. Also, for ‘root cause’ phrasing, keep it generic.

Devon Price (author): Confirmed. Templates contain no provider naming or RC specifics. This flow is strictly for in-incident updates; post-incident summaries are separate and will go through the disclosure checklist.

Miles Thornton (final): Approved.
Rafael Mendes (final): Approved.
Tomáš Novák (final): Approved.
Merged via squash after green CI.
release_notes: Internal tooling change: incident-bot now supports phase-based prompts and status update draft templates (v2) with required-field guardrails and next-update time normalization. Enable with `status_update_templates_version: v2`.
